verifications.claim: The Masters Green Jacket is awarded annually to the winner of the tournament at Augusta National Golf Club.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Come Sunday night at Augusta National Golf Club, someone will win the Masters green jacket'; R4: 'a green jacket ... has been awarded to the champion'; R3: 'awarded to the winner of The Masters'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state the green jacket is awarded annually to the Masters winner at Augusta National.

verifications.claim: Only 1 (sometimes 2) Masters Green Jacket is awarded each year.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'someone will win the Masters green jacket' (singular); R3: 'the green jacket to the winner'; R4: 'awarded to the champion' (one champion via playoff if needed)
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm one jacket awarded to the single annual winner; no mention of sometimes 2, contradicting the claim.

verifications.claim: Winners hold the Masters Green Jacket for a year before returning it to Augusta National Golf Club.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'That right is reserved only for the reigning champ after their victory. But when their year is up ... the jacket stays put'; R2: 'Once won, the reigning champion may take the jacket away from the club but only for one year. After this the jacket must remain at the club'; R4: 'must return it to the clubhouse one year after his victory'
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources explicitly state winners keep the jacket for one year before returning it.

verifications.claim: Winners holding the Masters Green Jacket for a year before returning it to Augusta National Golf Club symbolizes lifetime honorary membership.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'indicating the winners were to become honorary members of Augusta National'; R4: 'each Masters winner becomes an honorary member of the club'; R1: 'Jackets are reserved for club members and Masters winners'
verifications.reasoning: Sources link the green jacket directly to honorary lifetime membership for winners, with the one-year tradition as part of that symbolism.

verifications.claim: The Masters Green Jacket was introduced in 1937 to identify Augusta National Golf Club members.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'The club bought its first jackets from Brooks Uniform Company in 1937 ... so patrons could identify reliable sources of information'; R3: 'In 1937, Club officials started the custom of Augusta National members wearing a green blazer during Masters week so patrons could identify reliable sources of information'
verifications.reasoning: Sources precisely state introduction in 1937 for member identification during the tournament.

verifications.claim: The Masters Green Jacket is not for sale.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: Direct statement in R1 confirms jackets are not for sale.

verifications.claim: Augusta National Golf Club does not make Masters Green Jackets available to the public.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.reasoning: R1 explicitly states the club does not sell or make them available to the public.

verifications.claim: Only winners of the tournament at Augusta National Golf Club, Augusta National Golf Club members, and select individuals receive a Masters Green Jacket.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Jackets are reserved for club members and Masters winners. That’s it.'; R3: 'you must either win the Masters at Augusta National or be a member at Augusta National'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm only winners and members; 'select individuals' is broader/less precise and not explicitly supported.

verifications.claim: The winner can take the Masters Green Jacket home for the first year.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'That right is reserved only for the reigning champ after their victory'; R2: 'the reigning champion may take the jacket away from the club but only for one year'; R3: 'must be returned 12 months later'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm winners can take it home for the first year.

verifications.claim: After the first year, the Masters Green Jacket must remain on Augusta National Golf Club's grounds.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'don’t even think about taking them off the grounds ... when their year is up ... the jacket stays put'; R2: 'After this the jacket must remain at the club, only to be worn when revisiting'; R4: 'only a first-time and reigning champion may remove his jacket from the club grounds'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state jackets must stay on club grounds after one year, except when visiting.

verifications.claim: The Masters Green Jacket is officially "Masters Green" (Pantone 342).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'It’s Pantone 342, also known as Masters Green'; R3: 'The shade of its brilliant rye green is Pantone 342'; R4: 'Pantone 342C, "Augusta Green"'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly confirm the official color as Pantone 342, known as Masters Green.

verifications.claim: The Masters Green Jacket features a custom chest patch.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'the club logo on the left chest pocket'; R3: 'fitted with custom brass buttons inscribed with the Augusta National logo'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe the club logo on the left chest pocket, matching 'custom chest patch'.

verifications.claim: The Masters Green Jacket features brass buttons.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'it’s also on the brass buttons'; R3: 'fitted with custom brass buttons inscribed with the Augusta National logo'; R7: 'three brass buttons'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly mention brass buttons with the logo.

verifications.claim: Masters Green Jackets cannot be worn at just any function.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'There are certain times when Masters champions get to wear their jacket off grounds, but it’s only when they might be representing the tournament or club at a function or event, and of course, they’d need permission'; R7: 'Masters champions can do so only for one year ... never in conjunction with any commercial advertising'
verifications.reasoning: Sources state restrictions on wearing off-grounds, only for specific functions with permission.

verifications.claim: Masters Green Jackets are generally restricted to official, respectful appearances.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'only when they might be representing the tournament or club at a function or event, and of course, they’d need permission'; R7: 'allowed to wear his jacket to golf functions and appearances, but never in conjunction with any commercial advertising'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe restrictions to official/representative events, implying respectful contexts, but not precisely 'official, respectful appearances'.

verifications.claim: If a winner's Masters Green Jacket is damaged, it can be repaired or replaced by the original, official tailor.
verifications.label: OMITTED
verifications.reasoning: No sources mention repair or replacement policy for damaged jackets by the official tailor.
